name: Psychology of Learning and Instructional Design of AI-based Systems
description:
This tutorial offers a research-based insight into the psychological foundations of learning and into the design of AI-based teaching and learning systems – grounded in current and ongoing research from our group. Rather than treating theories in the abstract, we work along concrete studies of our own and show how questions from the psychology of learning and cognition are investigated empirically and translated into the design of learning environments.

Students gain insight into our research on topics such as professional vision, eye tracking and eye movement modeling examples, simulation-based learning, and the use of AI-based and adaptive systems in educational contexts. Using real examples from our research, it becomes tangible how we work: from theory-driven research questions through study design and data collection (including gaze and process data) to analysis and interpretation.

Key focus areas include:
– linking theories of learning to the design of AI-supported learning environments
– insights into current empirical research projects and their methodological approach
– how learning and perceptual processes can be measured and modeled
– opportunities, limitations, and ethical implications of AI-based systems in learning

In the tutorial, we discuss research findings, work with example material from our own studies, and jointly develop an understanding of how evidence-based design and empirical research are connected.
prerequisites: No specific prior knowledge is required. A general interest in empirical research on teaching and learning is helpful, as is a willingness to engage in inquiry-based, data-oriented work and to read academic literature in English. Active participation in discussion and group formats is expected.
